queries.title: Which recruiters are the hardest to crack?
queries.question: Among final-placement companies that have finished their process and attracted at least 20 applicants, which ones make offers to a SMALLER share of applicants than the campus-wide average? Students use this to decide where to spend their preparation time.
queries.concepts: 4-way join through a view, outer join (not every application has an offer), aggregate FILTER, GROUP BY, HAVING that compares a group aggregate with a scalar subquery.
queries.algebra:
γ company; count(*)→applicants, count(offer_id)→offers
( Application ⟕ Offer ⋈ JobDetails )
then σ applicants ≥ 20 ∧ offers/applicants < avg_rate
queries.sql:
SELECT d.company_name,
       d.sector,
       count(*)                                                AS applicants,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE iv.interviewed)                  AS interviewed,
       count(o.offer_id)                                       AS offers,
       count(o.offer_id) FILTER (WHERE o.status = 'ACCEPTED')  AS accepted,
       round(100.0 * count(o.offer_id) / count(*), 1)          AS offer_rate_pct
FROM application a
JOIN v_job_details d ON d.job_id = a.job_id
LEFT JOIN offer o    ON o.student_id = a.student_id AND o.job_id = a.job_id
LEFT JOIN LATERAL (SELECT TRUE AS interviewed
                   FROM interview i
                   WHERE i.student_id = a.student_id AND i.job_id = a.job_id
                   LIMIT 1) iv ON TRUE
WHERE d.cycle_type = 'FINAL'
  AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM offer x WHERE x.job_id = a.job_id)        -- process complete
GROUP BY d.company_id, d.company_name, d.sector
HAVING count(*) >= 20
   AND count(o.offer_id)::numeric / count(*) <
       (SELECT count(o2.offer_id)::numeric / count(*)                 -- campus-wide offer rate
        FROM application a2
        JOIN job_role j2 ON j2.job_id = a2.job_id
        LEFT JOIN offer o2 ON o2.student_id = a2.student_id AND o2.job_id = a2.job_id
        WHERE j2.cycle_id = 2
          AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM offer x WHERE x.job_id = a2.job_id))
ORDER BY offer_rate_pct

queries.title: Talent match for a newly posted job (relational division)
queries.question: Job 25 (Tidewater Logistics, Supply Chain Analytics Lead) has just been posted. Which students are eligible, not yet placed this cycle, and hold EVERY skill the job requires at the required level? The committee will nudge them to apply.
queries.concepts: Division expressed as "there is NO required skill that the student does NOT have" (double NOT EXISTS, two nested correlated subqueries), plus an anti-join for "not yet placed".
queries.algebra:
Qualified(student, skill) = π student,skill (σ proficiency ≥ min (StudentSkill ⋈ JobRequiredSkill_25))
Result = Qualified ÷ π skill (σ job_id = 25 (JobRequiredSkill))
queries.sql:
WITH params AS (SELECT 25 AS job_id)
SELECT s.roll_no,
       concat_ws(' ', p.first_name, p.last_name) AS student_name,
       pr.program_code,
       s.cgpa
FROM params
JOIN eligibility e ON e.job_id = params.job_id
JOIN student s     ON s.program_id = e.program_id
JOIN person p      ON p.person_id = s.person_id
JOIN program pr    ON pr.program_id = s.program_id
WHERE s.cgpa >= e.min_cgpa
  AND s.active_backlogs <= e.max_backlogs
  AND NOT s.opted_out
  -- division: no required skill exists ...
  AND NOT EXISTS (
        SELECT 1
        FROM job_required_skill r
        WHERE r.job_id = params.job_id
          -- ... that this student lacks at the required level
          AND NOT EXISTS (
                SELECT 1
                FROM student_skill ss
                WHERE ss.student_id  = s.person_id
                  AND ss.skill_id    = r.skill_id
                  AND ss.proficiency >= r.min_proficiency))
  -- anti-join: not already placed in this job's cycle
  AND NOT EXISTS (
        SELECT 1
        FROM offer o
        JOIN job_role j  ON j.job_id = o.job_id
        JOIN job_role jt ON jt.job_id = params.job_id
        WHERE o.student_id = s.person_id
          AND o.status = 'ACCEPTED'
          AND j.cycle_id = jt.cycle_id)
ORDER BY s.cgpa DESC

queries.title: Final-placement CTC leaderboard by program (window functions)
queries.question: For each program, who are the top 3 earners in final placements so far, how far above their program's average are they, and which pay quartile are they in? This feeds the placement report.
queries.concepts: Query over a VIEW (v_placement_status, a derived attribute); a named WINDOW with PARTITION BY + ORDER BY; DENSE_RANK (ties share a rank, no gaps), NTILE, AVG() OVER (aggregates without collapsing rows); a subquery to filter on a window result (WHERE cannot see it directly).
queries.note: DENSE_RANK gives tied CTCs the same rank; NTILE does not. It deals rows into 4 equal buckets, so two students with the same CTC can land in different quartiles. Use PERCENT_RANK() if ties must stay together.
queries.sql:
SELECT program_code, rank_in_program, roll_no, student_name, placed_with, ctc_lpa,
       program_avg_ctc, above_avg_by, pay_quartile, placed_in_program
FROM (
    SELECT program_code,
           roll_no,
           student_name,
           placed_with,
           ctc_lpa,
           DENSE_RANK() OVER w                                           AS rank_in_program,
           round(AVG(ctc_lpa) OVER (PARTITION BY program_code), 2)       AS program_avg_ctc,
           round(ctc_lpa - AVG(ctc_lpa) OVER (PARTITION BY program_code), 2) AS above_avg_by,
           NTILE(4) OVER w                                               AS pay_quartile,
           COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY program_code)                     AS placed_in_program
    FROM v_placement_status
    WHERE cycle_id = 2 AND placement_status = 'PLACED'
    WINDOW w AS (PARTITION BY program_code ORDER BY ctc_lpa DESC)
) ranked
WHERE rank_in_program <= 3
ORDER BY program_code, rank_in_program, roll_no

queries.title: Placement velocity: day-by-day cumulative progress
queries.question: During final placements, how many students from each program accepted an offer each day, and what share of each batch is placed by the end of each day? (The committee's daily progress chart.)
queries.concepts: Multiple CTEs; generate_series to build a calendar (so days with zero placements still appear); CROSS JOIN calendar x program; LEFT OUTER JOIN to the facts; running total with SUM() OVER (PARTITION BY ... ORDER BY ...).
queries.sql:
WITH calendar AS (
    SELECT d::date AS day
    FROM generate_series(DATE '2026-10-18', DATE '2026-10-28', INTERVAL '1 day') AS d
),
batch AS (
    SELECT pr.program_id, pr.program_code,
           count(*) FILTER (WHERE NOT s.opted_out) AS batch_size
    FROM program pr JOIN student s ON s.program_id = pr.program_id
    GROUP BY pr.program_id, pr.program_code
),
daily AS (
    SELECT s.program_id,
           (o.responded_at AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata')::date AS day,
           count(*) AS accepted
    FROM offer o
    JOIN job_role j ON j.job_id = o.job_id
    JOIN student s  ON s.person_id = o.student_id
    WHERE j.cycle_id = 2 AND o.status = 'ACCEPTED'
    GROUP BY s.program_id, (o.responded_at AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata')::date
)
SELECT c.day,
       b.program_code,
       COALESCE(dl.accepted, 0)                                         AS placed_today,
       SUM(COALESCE(dl.accepted, 0)) OVER run                           AS placed_cumulative,
       b.batch_size,
       round(100.0 * SUM(COALESCE(dl.accepted, 0)) OVER run / b.batch_size, 1) AS pct_batch_placed
FROM calendar c
CROSS JOIN batch b
LEFT JOIN daily dl ON dl.program_id = b.program_id AND dl.day = c.day
WINDOW run AS (PARTITION BY b.program_id ORDER BY c.day)
ORDER BY b.program_code, c.day

queries.title: Hidden gems: strong academics, lost in the interview room
queries.question: Which students are still unplaced in final placements even though, at a company that rejected them in an interview round, their CGPA was HIGHER than the average CGPA of the students that company selected? These students need interview coaching, not academic help, and the failed round says which kind.
queries.concepts: Correlated subquery (re-evaluated for each application row) used both in SELECT and in WHERE; LATERAL join to find the eliminating round; join on a composite key (job_id, round_no); built on a VIEW.
queries.sql:
SELECT ps.roll_no,
       ps.student_name,
       ps.program_code,
       ps.cgpa,
       d.company_name,
       elim.round_no || ' - ' || elim.round_type || ' (' || elim.result || ')' AS eliminated_in,
       (SELECT round(avg(s2.cgpa), 2)
        FROM offer o2 JOIN student s2 ON s2.person_id = o2.student_id
        WHERE o2.job_id = a.job_id)                                        AS selected_avg_cgpa
FROM v_placement_status ps
JOIN application a   ON a.student_id = ps.student_id AND a.status = 'REJECTED'
JOIN v_job_details d ON d.job_id = a.job_id AND d.cycle_id = ps.cycle_id
JOIN LATERAL (
        SELECT i.round_no, r.round_type, i.result
        FROM interview i
        JOIN interview_round r ON r.job_id = i.job_id AND r.round_no = i.round_no
        WHERE i.student_id = a.student_id AND i.job_id = a.job_id
          AND i.result IN ('NOT_CLEARED', 'ABSENT')) elim ON TRUE
WHERE ps.cycle_id = 2
  AND ps.placement_status IN ('UNPLACED', 'IN_PROCESS')
  AND ps.cgpa > (SELECT avg(s2.cgpa)                                       -- correlated on a.job_id
                 FROM offer o2 JOIN student s2 ON s2.person_id = o2.student_id
                 WHERE o2.job_id = a.job_id)
ORDER BY ps.cgpa DESC, d.company_name

tests.title: Every foreign key is backed by an index that can find its rows
tests.detail: PostgreSQL does not index FK columns automatically; an unindexed FK makes joins and ON DELETE checks scan the whole child table. Covered means: an index whose leading columns are exactly the FK columns, or a UNIQUE index on a leading subset of them (e.g. PK job_id covers FK (job_id, role_type)).
